catalog_quote: In Vamale, disyllabic words have penultimate stress, as is typical in Oceanic settings. Trisyllabic, morphologically simple, non-derived nouns take stress on the first syllable, see Table 5.10. These are rare, though loanwords now increase their number. ... Longer words are morphologically complex and have stress on the penultimate stress-bearing unit, which is often a syllable of the root, but not always. While some morphological factors complicate the picture, regular phonological aspects predict most stress positions. A closed syllable will be stressed over an open one, a fortis onset will usually top a tenuis onset, and a long syllable will be stressed above all else. This gives us a hierarchy of factors: (16) Long syllable > fortis onset > closed syllable > penultimate syllable ... For Hmwaveke, stress is described as being fundamentally penultimate (Campbell 1987: 59) ... Campbell…

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The deciding quotation, the hierarchy (16), the extrametricality passage and the overview quote are all verbatim in the LangSci PDF we hold/text at the stated sections and pages (5.6 pp. 80-82; 1.1 pp. 2-3; 5.3.1 pp. 74-75). The source is a 2024 open-access reference grammar (published PhD) with a dedicated stress section, and it is the only modern description of Vamale per Glottolog (1 descriptive ref) and per the grammar's own survey of previous work; no phonology article or instrumental study exists that I could find. The weight-hedged coding (penultimate/initial default overridden by long vowel > fortis onset > closed syllable, with author's 'usually'/'most' hedges and morphological extrametricality) faithfully reflects the source. The only conceivable addition is Campbell's 1987 MA thesis on the sister variety Hmwaveke, which offers a competing penultimate-stress-causes-length analysis

sources.note: Only other stress account in the Vamale/Hmwaveke dialect pair: Rohleder (pp. 74-75, 82) reports Campbell analyses Hmwaveke stress as fundamentally penultimate with vowel length a consequence of stress, the reverse of Rohleder's 'length attracts stress' on which our weight-hedged coding rests. Strictly about the western variety (Hmwaveke, ISO mrk, separate glottocode), so it would annotate rather than reclassify this record.
